title: Isaiah Chapter 33 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 33 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 33 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 33.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:1 say about those who deal treacherously?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:1 states that those who spoil will themselves be spoiled when they cease their actions.

questions.question: Who is asked to be gracious in Isaiah 33:2?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:2 directly addresses the LORD, asking Him to be gracious.

questions.question: What happens at the noise of the tumult according to Isaiah 33:3?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:3 states that at the noise of the tumult, the people fled.

questions.question: What will happen to the spoil according to Isaiah 33:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:4 mentions that the spoil shall be gathered like the gathering of the caterpiller.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:5, what has the LORD filled Zion with?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:5 states that the LORD has filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Wisdom and knowledge are described as the stability of times in Isaiah 33:6.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:6 states that wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.

questions.question: What do the ambassadors of peace do according to Isaiah 33:7?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:7 states that the ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly.

questions.question: True or False: The highways lie waste according to Isaiah 33:8.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:8 mentions that the highways lie waste and the wayfaring man ceaseth.

questions.question: In Isaiah 33, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Behold, their valiant ones shall cry
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:1 is the first instruction given in this chapter.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:9 say about the earth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:9 states that the earth mourneth and languisheth.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will save us according to Isaiah 33:22.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:22 affirms that the LORD is our judge, lawgiver, and king, and He will save us.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:11, what shall ye conceive?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:11 states that ye shall conceive chaff and bring forth stubble.

questions.question: What is described as a treasure in Isaiah 33:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:6 states that the fear of the LORD is His treasure.

questions.question: What happens to the inhabitants in Isaiah 33:24?
options: They shall not say, I am sick
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not say, I am sick
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:24 mentions that the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 33:10 mentions that the LORD will rise and be exalted.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:10 states that the LORD says He will rise and be exalted.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 33 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 33 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to those who deal treacherously according to Isaiah 33:1?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:1 states, 'when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.' This indicates that those who act treacherously will face consequences for their actions.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:2, what do the people ask the Lord to be in times of trouble?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:2 says, 'O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.' This verse shows the people's dependence on God for strength and salvation.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:5 indicate about the Lord's presence in Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:5 states, 'The LORD is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.' This emphasizes God's role in establishing justice and right living.

questions.question: What is said about wisdom and knowledge in Isaiah 33:6?
options: They are the stability of thy times
questions.correctAnswer: They are the stability of thy times
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:6 mentions, 'And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure.' This highlights the importance of wisdom and knowledge in providing stability and strength.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:10 say the Lord will do?
options: He will rise and be exalted
questions.correctAnswer: He will rise and be exalted
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:10 declares, 'Now will I rise, saith the LORD; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself.' This signifies God's authority and power being made known.

questions.question: What does it mean that the people will be as the burnings of lime according to Isaiah 33:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:12 states, 'And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.' This illustrates the fate of those who do not follow God's ways.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:14, who is afraid?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:14 says, 'The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites.' This shows the fear that grips those who live in sin.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:15 say about the person who walks righteously?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:15 describes the qualities of a righteous person, indicating that such a person will dwell on high and be protected, which implies blessings.

questions.question: What promise is given in Isaiah 33:16 regarding the righteous?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:16 states, 'He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.' This emphasizes the security and provision for the righteous.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 33:19 says that the people will see a fierce people with a deeper speech than they can perceive.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:19 states, 'Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive...' This indicates that they will not encounter a fierce people.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 33:24 promises that the inhabitants will say, 'I am sick.'
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:24 states, 'And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.' This indicates health and forgiveness rather than sickness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 33:20 describes Jerusalem as a quiet habitation that shall not be taken down.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:20 states, '...thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down...' This emphasizes the stability and permanence of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:13 instruct those who are near to do regarding God's might?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:13 says, 'Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.' This underscores the importance of recognizing God's power.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 33:14 connect to the call for righteousness in verse 33:15?
options: It reinforces the need for fear
It dismisses the need for holiness
It highlights the consequences of sin
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the consequences of sin
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:14 speaks of the fear of sinners, while Isaiah 33:15 describes the characteristics of the righteous. This connection shows the dire consequences of living in sin versus the blessings of righteousness.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 33 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 33.

questions.question: What will the inhabitants of Zion see according to Isaiah 33:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:17 states, 'Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off,' indicating that the focus will be on witnessing the king's beauty.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:22, who is described as our judge, lawgiver, and king?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:22 clearly states, 'For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us,' emphasizing the role of the LORD in governance and salvation.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:24 say about the inhabitants of the land?
options: They will not say, I am sick
questions.correctAnswer: They will not say, I am sick
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:24 states, 'And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity,' suggesting health and forgiveness for the inhabitants.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the fear of the LORD is his treasure' in Isaiah 33:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:6 mentions that 'wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times,' indicating that the fear of the LORD is foundational for stability.

questions.question: In Isaiah 33:13, who is called to hear what the LORD has done?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:13 states, 'Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might,' addressing both groups.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:19, what kind of people will not be seen?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:19 states, 'Thou shalt not see a fierce people,' indicating the absence of hostility for those in Zion.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the structure of Isaiah 33:22 where the roles of the LORD are listed?
questions.explanation: The use of parallelism in Isaiah 33:22 emphasizes the three roles of the LORD: judge, lawgiver, and king, highlighting their interconnectedness.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament echoes the theme of the LORD as our king and savior found in Isaiah 33:22?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:10-11 states that every knee shall bow to Jesus, affirming His lordship, similar to Isaiah's proclamation of the LORD as king.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:18 refer to when speaking of the heart meditating terror?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:18 states, 'Thine heart shall meditate terror,' indicating a deep awareness of the judgment and consequences of sin.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:15, who is described as walking righteously?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:15 defines the righteous as 'He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly,' highlighting the qualities of righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 33:5 states that the LORD is exalted because He dwells on high.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:5 affirms, 'The LORD is exalted; for he dwelleth on high,' establishing His supremacy and exalted nature.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 33:20 describes Zion as a place that can be taken down.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:20 states that Jerusalem is a quiet habitation, 'a tabernacle that shall not be taken down,' indicating its permanence.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'wisdom' as used in Isaiah 33:6?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'wisdom' in this context implies discernment, which is essential for stability during tumultuous times, as stated in Isaiah 33:6.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:9 say about the state of the earth and its regions?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:9 states, 'The earth mourneth and languisheth,' indicating desolation and despair in the face of judgment.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 33 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 33 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:1 indicate about those who spoil others?
options: They will be spoiled when they cease their actions
questions.correctAnswer: They will be spoiled when they cease their actions
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:1 states that those who spoil will themselves be spoiled once they cease their treachery, highlighting the principle of divine justice.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:5, what has the LORD filled Zion with?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:5 reveals that the LORD has filled Zion with judgment and righteousness, emphasizing His sovereignty and moral order.

questions.question: What is described as the stability of thy times in Isaiah 33:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:6 states that wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of the times, indicating their essential role in salvation and security.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:13 call upon those who are far off to do?
options: Repent and turn to the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:13 urges those far off to acknowledge God's might, highlighting the universal recognition of His power.

questions.question: Who shall dwell on high according to Isaiah 33:16?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:16 specifies that he who walks righteously and speaks uprightly will dwell on high, indicating the blessings of righteousness.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:24 say about the inhabitants of Zion?
options: They will be in constant fear
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:24 promises that the inhabitants shall not say, 'I am sick,' indicating divine healing and forgiveness of iniquity.

questions.question: What does the earth do in Isaiah 33:9?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:9 depicts the earth as mourning and languishing, reflecting the devastation and judgment upon the land.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Isaiah 33:10?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:10 shows God's sovereignty as He declares His intention to rise and be exalted, demonstrating His ultimate authority.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 33:22 and 33:5 convey about God's role in Zion?
options: He is judge, lawgiver, and king
He is distant from His people
He is indifferent to moral order
questions.correctAnswer: He is judge, lawgiver, and king
questions.explanation: The combination of Isaiah 33:22 and 33:5 shows that God fulfills the roles of judge, lawgiver, and king, establishing justice and righteousness in Zion.

questions.question: What do Isaiah 33:17 and 33:19 suggest about the future vision of the people?
options: They will see the king in his beauty
They will see their enemies prevail
questions.correctAnswer: They will see the king in his beauty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:17 promises that the people's eyes shall see the king in his beauty, indicating a hopeful and glorious future.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:8 say about the state of the highways?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:8 indicates that the highways lie waste, symbolizing the breakdown of order and the consequences of betrayal.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 33:14 say about sinners in Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:14 reveals that the sinners in Zion are afraid, indicating the recognition of impending judgment and their guilt.

questions.question: What does the imagery of thorns and fire in Isaiah 33:12 represent?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:12 uses the imagery of thorns and fire to symbolize the destructive consequences of sin and divine judgment.

questions.question: What is the main theme of Isaiah 33 in relation to God’s judgment and salvation?
options: The call to repentance and assurance of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The call to repentance and assurance of salvation
questions.explanation: The overall theme of Isaiah 33 emphasizes God's judgment against sin while offering hope for salvation to the righteous, calling for repentance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is uninvolved in human affairs. What does Isaiah 33:22 teach regarding God's role?
options: He is distant from His creation
He is actively involved as judge, lawgiver, and king
questions.correctAnswer: He is actively involved as judge, lawgiver, and king
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:22 asserts that the LORD is our judge, lawgiver, and king, showing His active involvement and authority in the affairs of humanity.
